title: Observability weekly notes - 2026-06-08
content:
Week: 2026-06-01 - 2026-06-07
Author: Maya Chen (owner)
Attendees: Arjun, Leah, Ben, Priya, Tomas, Maya

Summary:
This week focused on shipping incremental tracing improvements (sampling + span enrichment), completing the Grafana dashboard migration for the infra-cost workspace, and finishing the first pass of cost-telemetry exports to BigQuery. We saw initial cost savings from smarter sampling on the lowest-value services, and found a couple of dashboard queries that were driving excessive cardinality.

Standup highlights / Daily notes:
- 2026-06-01 (Mon):
  - Tracing: Arjun validated reduced CPU overhead with sampling set to 0.05 for background batch jobs; end-to-end test shows ~12% CPU reduction on the job fleet (PR #378).
  - Dashboards: Leah started migrating infra-cost Grafana panels to the new datasource; identified 3 panels with unbounded tag expansions.
  - Cost telemetry: Priya validated BigQuery export schema and started ingesting 48h of sample data.

- 2026-06-03 (Wed):
  - Tracing: Canary rollout to 10% of traffic for web frontends; p95 trace ingestion latency increased by +40ms on one host group - investigated and reverted sampler config for that group.
  - Dashboards: Fixed two heavy TSDB queries by adding pre-aggregations; dashboard load time improved from ~14s -> ~3.6s for infra-cost overview.
  - Cost telemetry: Tomas added labels for model-version and route in exported rows; this enables per-route cost KPIs in BigQuery.

- 2026-06-05 (Fri):
  - Tracing: Rolled out adaptive sampling to 30% traffic after addressing the host group regression. Monitored for 24h - no new regressions observed.
  - Dashboards: Completed migration of infra-cost workspace panels; left one experimental panel (high-card panel) for follow-up.
  - Cost telemetry: Initial queries show ~12k USD/monthable estimated savings if caching + batching flags reduce token counts by 6% on observed routes.

Action items / Owners:
- Arjun: Finalize sampler config docs and add automated canary checks (due 2026-06-15).
- Leah: Replace experimental high-card panel with pre-aggregated table query; follow up with frontend for possible tag limits (due 2026-06-12).
- Priya: Run 7-day BigQuery export validation and build first per-route cost dashboard (due 2026-06-14).
- Tomas: Add unit tests for label extraction pipeline and validate no-schema-drift on export (due 2026-06-11).
- Ben: Draft runbook for tracing ingestion regressions (short-term mitigation steps) and share with SRE (due 2026-06-10).

Blockers / Risks:
- A host group showed increased trace ingestion latency during the initial sampler canary; root cause appears to be a combination of sampler config and an old agent version. Mitigation: pin sampler config per-agent version for canaries and schedule agent upgrades.
- One Grafana panel still expands tags unboundedly and causes high query cost. This is a medium-priority risk for dashboard load spikes during reports.
- Cost telemetry: need guardrails for PII/PII-like labels in exported rows; legal is reviewing export schema (Priya coordinating).

Metrics & Observability signals:
- Tracing ingestion: p50 ingestion latency ~120ms, p95 ~360ms (after canary rollback fixed regression).
- Sampling effects (canary -> 30%): observed token-span count decrease ~28% for background jobs; CPU on those jobs down ~12%.
- Dashboard performance: infra-cost overview panel load 14s -> 3.6s after pre-aggregation.
- Cost telemetry: first 48h export shows route-level breakdowns consistent with internal billing; early estimate: $12k/mo potential savings if caching/quantization guidance applied to top 20% of routes by volume.

Incidents / Postmortems:
- 2026-06-03 tracing-canary-regression: brief regression in p95 ingestion latency for host-group a1. No customer-facing outages. Postmortem in progress (JIRA-OBS-452).

Decisions / Notes:
- Default sampling recommendation: adaptive sampler with base-rate 0.05 for background jobs, 0.2 for web frontends, and per-route overrides. Docs to be updated in Confluence.
- Export schema approved for non-PII labels; legal to sign off on final field list before wider export.
- We will schedule a dashboard cost review with Finance next week to prioritize panels to keep vs. archive.

Follow-ups for next week (2026-06-08 -> 2026-06-14):
- Complete sampler docs + canary automation (Arjun).
- Finish dashboard pre-aggregation and reduce cardinality panels (Leah).
- Validate full 7-day BigQuery export and ship per-route cost dashboard MVP (Priya + Tomas).
- Runbook + alert knobs for tracing ingestion regressions (Ben + SRE).
- Prepare short presentation for GTM on cost telemetry capabilities and expected run-rate savings (Maya + Product).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep list of heavy TSDB queries; we might want to migrate some to reporting pipelines in StatsDB.
- Check whether model-version label cardinality can be reduced by using a hashed prefix or bucketing strategy.
- Quick follow-up: confirm agent upgrade rollout plan with release-engineering so canaries are done on upgraded agent binaries only.

Attachments / links:
- Tracing sampler proposal (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tracing+Sampling+Proposal
- Canary regression ticket: JIRA-OBS-452
- PR with sampler + instrumentation fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/378
- Slack thread for canary discussion: https://slack-redwood.slack.com/archives/C01OBS1234/p1650000000000000

End of notes.
